title: Chicken or turkey with potatoes and vegetables without carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens, no sauce

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of roasted or boiled chicken or turkey, potatoes and a selection of vegetables, excluding carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens. It is prepared without any sauces, making it light and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey provide complete protein containing all essential amino acids.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed root vegetables and are rich in vitamin C and potassium.
Excluding carrots and broccoli reduces beta‑carotene content while retaining other vitamins and minerals from the remaining vegetables.
A sauce‑free preparation is suitable for people monitoring salt and sugar intake.
When stored properly, the ingredients stay fresh for 3‑4 days in the refrigerator.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Poultry meat supplies high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Potassium and magnesium
items.content: Potatoes and vegetables provide potassium and magnesium, supporting heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin B6
items.content: Chicken and turkey are high in vitamin B6, which is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: The absence of sauces and sweet ingredients makes the dish suitable for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables and potatoes add dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to proteins found in chicken or turkey.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the meat was pre‑salted, sodium levels can be high; use minimal added salt.

items.title: Potential bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked poultry may harbor pathogens; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: Foodborne illness from improperly stored vegetables
items.content: Vegetables left at room temperature for more than 2 hours can become a source of bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course, or pair it with whole‑grain sides such as quinoa or brown rice. Vegetables can be served in large chunks or mashed, and the meat sliced into strips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then place it in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat to at least 75 °C before serving.
